coverage: Eight stories · software security, AI evidence, drones, digital culture, accessibility, robotics and student computing

cards.headline: MCP Python SDK fixes two memory-exhaustion flaws
cards.summary: Maintainers of the official Model Context Protocol Python SDK published two high-severity advisories about servers using too much memory. One involved sessions that were not reclaimed; another involved HTTP request bodies with no size limit. Patched releases add limits and cleanup.
cards.whyItMatters: Software security includes protecting a system's resources, not just passwords and data. Limits on memory, request size and session lifetime can keep a service available when inputs behave unexpectedly.

csp.connection: Network services must manage finite resources and validate incoming data so one client cannot consume everything.

cards.headline: AI rewrites petitions without improving their results
cards.summary: Cornell researchers analyzed 1.5 million Change.org petitions around the rollout of an AI writing assistant. AI-assisted petitions became longer and used more similar wording, but the researchers found little or no improvement in outcomes such as comments and signatures.
cards.whyItMatters: A tool can noticeably change an output without making it more effective. Large real-world datasets can test whether an AI feature actually helps people accomplish the goal it was designed for.

csp.connection: Researchers compared large groups of platform data to measure how a computing feature changed both text and user outcomes.

cards.headline: Student-built drones search disaster zones without GPS
cards.summary: University teams in the NATO-supported SAPIENCE competition tested autonomous drones in a simulated disaster area without GPS or human control. The aircraft had to navigate, find simulated survivors, judge urgency, coordinate supplies and avoid obstacles and one another.
cards.whyItMatters: Autonomous machines need sensing, navigation, communication and decision-making to work together. The project also shows students debugging real systems when networks and hardware do not behave exactly as expected.

csp.connection: Robotic systems combine sensors, software and network communication to coordinate actions in the physical world.

cards.headline: TikTok turns a music release into a group challenge
cards.summary: TikTok launched an in-app hub around Taylor Swift's “Patient Zero” with phased unlocks, a profile-frame reward and group goals that reveal behind-the-scenes clips. Some rewards depend on actions such as following accounts, posting with the song or listening to tracks.
cards.whyItMatters: Apps can turn media into an interactive system using progress, rewards and collective goals. Those interface choices can shape what users do, share and listen to rather than simply showing them content.

csp.connection: Platform design choices can influence participation, sharing and how online communities experience media.

cards.headline: AI coding tools stumble on web accessibility
cards.summary: Accessibility company AudioEye asked five AI coding tools to build three websites each to meet WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility requirements. AudioEye reports that all 15 test sites failed even the basic Level A tier; the company sells accessibility services, so its study is best read as a vendor test rather than independent research.
cards.whyItMatters: Code that looks correct can still fail for keyboard or screen-reader users. Whether code comes from a person or an AI tool, testing with accessibility requirements and real interactions remains part of building usable software.

csp.connection: Developers test and revise computing products to meet user needs, including needs that may not be visible on screen.

cards.headline: Oarfish fins inspire a quieter underwater robot
cards.summary: Cornell researchers studied how oarfish move hundreds of dorsal-fin rays in coordinated waves, using dissections, X-rays, CT scans and video. The work is helping inform a proposed large underwater robot that could move quietly while carrying instruments to monitor ocean health.
cards.whyItMatters: Engineers often study biological systems before designing machines. Turning a fish's motion into a robot requires converting observations into mechanical structures, control rules and sensor-driven behavior.

csp.connection: A robot needs programmed control patterns to coordinate many moving parts and produce a desired motion.

cards.headline: Lost student Moon photos get a permanent archive
cards.summary: Cornell's Spacecraft Planetary Image Facility is preserving recovered MoonKAM photos requested by middle-school students during NASA's 2011–12 GRAIL mission. The images were not originally required to be archived, and some sets had become difficult to locate.
cards.whyItMatters: Digital data can disappear even when the original project was important. Archives need deliberate storage, organization and long-term stewardship so future students and researchers can still find and use old data.

csp.connection: Computing systems store and organize digital information, but preservation depends on decisions about formats, metadata and long-term access.

cards.headline: High-school students train in Python and AI
cards.summary: An NSF-funded Broward College program is bringing AI, IT and cybersecurity training to first-year college students and students at Nova High School. Its pathways include entry-level Python, data analytics and AI credentials, plus hands-on mentoring and problem-based learning.
cards.whyItMatters: Computer science skills can connect directly to many kinds of work, not only jobs labeled “programmer.” The program is an example of schools building practical pathways from high school into computing and technology careers.

csp.connection: Computing knowledge affects education and career pathways across industries, including jobs that mix technology with other fields.
